correctness.rationale: For n=2..6 every ternary word is generated and checked for self-bifix, every surviving pair for both oriented cross-bifix overlaps and Hamming distance >=3; this gives an if-and-only-if with compatibility cliques. Python Bron-Kerbosch enumerates all maximal cliques (414 candidates and 24,156 edges at n=6, with exactly 528 maximal 8-cliques and no larger), while independent C++17 increasing-order enumeration counts all cliques and independently obtains maximal sizes 1,1,2,4,8 and maximum-code counts 6,18,108,300,528. Complete optimal-code tables and all alphabet-permutation/reversal orbits were checked. Two explicit codebook witnesses are listed. Scope finite n<=6; no extrapolation.

value.rationale: A natural joint constraint in block codes is cross-bifix self-synchronization plus Hamming-distance-three one-substitution correction. The exact minimum length six for transmitting eight ternary messages (3 bits) gives a meaningful short-block threshold, while 528 six-symbol optimal designs in 49 equivalence classes and rigid equidistance of every five-symbol optimum supply design and classification data. The complete reproducible finite benchmark is a substantive constrained-channel invariant without depending on a general asymptotic theorem.
